newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Adecco 1996 group sales up nine pct.
newsitem.headline: Adecco 1996 group sales up nine pct.

text.p: Temporary employment firm Adecco SA said total group sales for the year 1996 rose nine percent to 8.524 billion Swiss francs from 7.830 billiion in 1995.
It also said that sales for the fourth quarter, to December 29, 1996, were 2.257 billion. That compared with 1.869 billion in the 1995 period, making a gain of 21 percent.
The sales total for the fourth quarter did not include cleaning and security divisions which were sold in September 1996.

"In view of the challenging economic situation in France, Germany and Switzerland, we are satisfied with the overall development of Adecco," said Adecco's chief executive officer John Bowmer in a statement released with the company's results.

The company said it was confident that revenues in France would benefit from Adecco's new presence. The company was formed through a merger last year of Swiss temporary employment firm Adia SA and French firm Ecco SA.
It said France's economy would continue to pose a challenge, but revenues were steady in French franc terms.

Adecco said that fourth quarter sales in France, in Swiss franc terms, rose eight percent to 959 billion from 889 billion in the 1995 fourth quarter. Sales for the entire year were virtually unchanged at 3.812 billion versus 3.829 billion.

"Apart from business in France, business in the rest of Europe, with a gain in revenue of 29 percent, went exceedingly well," Adecco said, refering to fourth quarter sales. For the year, non-French European sales rose 23 percent.

North American sales showed a strong gain of 26 percent for the quarter and 21 percent for the year. Asia/Pacific sales made a strong recovery from the third quarter, it said. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
